title: Mach42 Delivers a Different Take on AI in the Design Flow at DAC 2026 - Semiwiki
gist: At DAC 2026, EDA's AI narrative flipped from bolting AI onto existing tools to trained models actively driving design decisions, and Mach42 — an Oxford physics spinout that pivoted from fusion simulation — is applying 'Physics AI' surrogate models to analog verification, the segment that has gone from 10% to 40% of chip respins in twenty years. The pitch is not replacing SPICE but ~100x wider design-space coverage that tells teams where to point SPICE.

insights.claim: DAC 2026 marked a shift in EDA from AI being added to traditional tools to improve existing methodologies, toward trained AI models taking an active role in design and optimization themselves.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: A change in the unit of competition in EDA: incumbents selling AI-accelerated point tools face entrants selling AI that decides what to design, which is a different moat and a different pricing model.
insights.quote: I believe DAC 2026 will be remembered as the turning point for AI assisted design.

insights.claim: The differentiator among new AI-native EDA entrants is a focus on WHAT should be done in a design rather than HOW to make an existing process incrementally better.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: A quick screen for AI-EDA pitches: tools that only speed up an existing step compete on cost, tools that expand the searched design space compete on outcomes and command more value.
insights.quote: A stronger focus on WHAT should be done instead of HOW to make an existing process better.
insights.locator: A stronger focus on WHAT should be done

insights.claim: Multiple new companies presented fundamentally new AI-driven chip design approaches at DAC 2026, indicating a cohort of entrants rather than a single-vendor story.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Watch for a wave of AI-EDA startup funding and acquisition targets; incumbent EDA vendors typically buy rather than build in these cycles.
insights.locator: There were several new companies that highlighted

insights.claim: Even amid a wave of new AI design approaches, analog/mixed-signal design remains structurally different from digital and is not addressed by the same AI techniques.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Analog is a separate, defensible AI-EDA submarket; general digital-design AI leaders do not automatically win it.
insights.quote: All this new technology does share something that isn’t new however – analog/mixed signal design is different.

themes.theme: Analog is now the dominant respin cause

insights.claim: Per Siemens/Wilson Research data cited at DAC 2026, digital blocks caused 40% of chip respins in 2005 and only 15% in 2025, while analog blocks went from 10% to 40% of respins over the same period.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: The cost of failure has migrated to analog; verification spend and tool budgets should follow, favoring vendors positioned in analog verification.
insights.quote: In 2025, digital contributes 15% to respins while analog contributes 40%.

insights.claim: Analog content in advanced chips is growing materially, with the Apple M4 Max cited as containing about 200 instances of 20 different analog blocks.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Analog verification workload scales with instance count, not just block variety — a concrete demand driver for analog-focused EDA tooling at leading-edge SoC vendors.
insights.quote: the Apple M4 Max has about 200 instances of 20 different analog blocks
insights.locator: Bijan began by reviewing the increasing analog content

insights.claim: Analog verification is currently the limiting factor on many chip project schedules, making it the bottleneck a design-productivity tool should attack.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Time-to-market leverage in SoC development now sits in analog verification; solving it has outsized schedule value and therefore pricing power.
insights.quote: a process that is currently the limiting factor for many projects

insights.claim: Generative AI is insufficient for analog design because it automates workflows by learning patterns and generating code and scripts, whereas analog needs exploration of the design space itself.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: A caution against valuing LLM-wrapper EDA plays as if they solve analog; the binding constraint is simulation throughput, not code authoring.
insights.quote: Bijan went on to point out that generative AI isn’t enough.
insights.locator: Bijan went on to point out

insights.claim: Mach42's Physics AI learns circuit dynamics to predict circuit behavior, removing time-consuming analog simulation from the loop during design exploration.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: A surrogate-model architecture: value accrues from replacing simulator compute cycles, which is a direct substitution against EDA compute and hardware spend.
insights.quote: Mach42’s Physics AI learns circuit dynamics which then allows prediction of circuit behavior.
insights.locator: He explained that Mach42’s Physics AI

insights.claim: Traditional analog verification relies on non-linear equation solvers that are highly accurate but extremely slow, and the industry's main speedup lever has been throwing more and faster hardware at the problem.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: If AI surrogates displace brute-force compute, the incremental hardware demand from analog verification farms is at risk — a second-order negative for compute-scaling narratives in EDA.
insights.quote: The main method of speedup is to apply more and faster hardware to the problem.
insights.locator: Traditional methods use non-linear equation solvers

insights.claim: Mach42 trains its analog models on proven, accurate simulation results from popular existing simulation tools rather than on design source data.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Training data is generated per-design by the customer's own licensed simulators, which sidesteps IP-sharing objections but keeps the approach dependent on incumbent simulator licenses.
insights.quote: Model training data is based on proven, accurate simulation results from popular tools.

themes.theme: Oxford physics spinout pivoting from fusion to silicon

insights.claim: Mach42 was spun out of the University of Oxford Department of Physics in 2019 to accelerate expensive physics simulations, was applied to emulating extreme states of matter such as plasmas, and won initial contracts in fusion energy before pivoting.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: The core IP is general surrogate modeling of physical systems, so semiconductor EDA may be the first commercial beachhead rather than the total addressable market.

insights.claim: Mach42 took seed funding in 2021 and only then redirected from fusion-energy simulation to complex analog circuit verification, identifying it as a fundamental simulation bottleneck.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: A 2021-seeded company presenting production demos at DAC 2026 implies a maturing, fundable cohort — relevant timing for later-stage AI-EDA investment.

themes.theme: Demo mechanics and the SPICE division of labor

insights.claim: In a live DAC 2026 demo, an LDO design was loaded into Virtuoso Studio ADE to generate training data, and the trained Mach42 model then produced 1,000 waveforms across a parameter sweep in literally a few seconds.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: A concrete throughput datapoint from an eyewitness demo, not a datasheet claim — the kind of evidence that precedes real design-win announcements.
insights.quote: In literally a few seconds there were 1,000 waveforms available.

insights.claim: Mach42's trained models let a verification team cover roughly 100x more of the design space surface where failure modes are likely, so SPICE can be focused on those regions rather than run broadly.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: The quantified value proposition — 100x coverage, not 100x speed — reframes ROI as escaped-bug and respin avoidance rather than license-cost savings.
insights.quote: deliver around 100x the design space coverage surface where the failure modes are likely to be
insights.locator: The performance of the trained model enables a verification team

insights.claim: Mach42 positions its AI as complementary rather than displacing, explicitly leaving SPICE as the signoff authority while AI decides which corners SPICE should be run at.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Non-displacing positioning shortens the sales cycle by avoiding signoff-liability objections, but it also caps the revenue pool since incumbent SPICE licenses stay in place.
insights.quote: SPICE remains the sign off authority; Analog Intelligence just makes sure it is deployed at the right corners.
insights.locator: The performance of the trained model enables a verification team

insights.claim: The generated waveform output includes explicit upper and lower bounds on the predicted data, giving users a visible accuracy envelope on the AI model's predictions.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Calibrated uncertainty is the practical prerequisite for engineers trusting a surrogate model in a signoff-adjacent flow; its presence is a maturity marker to check in competing tools.
insights.quote: you will see upper and lower bounds for the generated data
insights.locator: If you look closely at the figure above

insights.claim: Model setup and training in the Mach42 flow is described as straightforward and not time-consuming, with a GUI defining operating points and multi-variable relationships to keep simulated points within real operating conditions.
insights.speaker: Mike Gianfagna
insights.so_what: Low setup cost per design is what determines whether a per-design surrogate model approach can scale across the ~200 analog instances in a modern SoC.
insights.quote: The process is straightforward and not time-consuming.
insights.locator: How the data should be assembled
